test_title: PYST 2: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 07 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following factors best explains the formation of ox-bow lakes along river courses?

options.text: Sudden uplift of riverbeds by tectonic activity
Lateral erosion on the outer banks and deposition on the inner banks

solution:
The Correct answer is __**Lateral erosion on the outer banks and deposition on the inner banks**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ox-bow lakes** are formed due to the **meandering nature of rivers**, which is a natural process in the middle and lower courses of rivers.
 
• **Lateral erosion** occurs on the **outer banks** of a river bend, where the velocity of water is higher, causing the banks to erode and the bend to become more pronounced over time.
 
• At the same time, **deposition** happens on the **inner banks** of the bend, where the water velocity is lower, leading to the accumulation of sediments.
 
• This process eventually creates an extreme curve in the river, and when the neck of the meander becomes very narrow, the river may cut through it during a flood or high flow event, forming a new, straighter channel.
 
• The abandoned meander loop, isolated from the main river, forms an **ox-bow lake**.
 
• Ox-bow lakes are characteristic features of **low-lying floodplains** where rivers flow gently.
 
• This process is a combination of **fluvial erosion and deposition**, driven by the natural dynamics of the flowing water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sudden uplift of riverbeds by tectonic activity**__

 __
 
• **Tectonic activity** can alter river courses, but it does not typically result in the formation of **ox-bow lakes**.
 
• Sudden uplift may lead to the formation of features like **waterfalls** or **gorges**, but not ox-bow lakes.
 
 
 
• **Tectonic uplift disrupting the flow**__
 __
 
• **Tectonic uplift** can modify river systems by creating ** or altering gradients, but this process is not related to the creation of ox-bow lakes**.
 
 
 
• **Glacial retreat leaving depressions**__
 
 
• **Glacial retreat** can lead to the formation of features like **kettle lakes** and **moraines**, which are different from ox-bow lakes formed in fluvial systems.
 
• This process is associated with glacial landscapes rather than river meandering.
